-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

1	# Your task
2	
3	Design and build a back-end product of your own invention: a web service, spoken to over HTTP with JSON, that many people
4	use at once. Each person signs in and works with records that are theirs alone. Use C# on ASP.NET Core with the .NET 10
5	SDK (10.0.401), and keep the data with EF Core in SQLite through the package `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite`.
6	
7	## The product
8	
9	Invent it. These subjects are taken and may not be used: habits, streaks, check-ins or reminders; tickets; runs; jobs;
10	notes; expenses, expense reports, reimbursements or payouts. Choose a subject that has real rules in it.
11	
12	Whatever you invent must include all of the following:
13	
14	- 10 to 16 HTTP routes in total, among them one where a person signs in with a name and a password;
15	- seeded people with at least two different roles, and at least one route that only one of those roles may use;
16	- at least two kinds of record that belong to the person who is signed in, so that no one can see or change somebody
17	  else's;
18	- at least one kind of record that belongs to a person only by way of a record it sits under;
19	- at least one stored value that the service keeps but never sends back in any answer;
20	- one record with a lifecycle: a state that changes at least twice over its life, where some changes are refused in
21	  some states;
22	- checking of what clients send, so that a request with a missing value or a value out of range is turned away.
23	
24	## The code is yours
25	
26	How the code is structured, and how each requirement above is met, are your decisions alone. Decide as you would for
27	a real product that is going to keep growing. The two documents beside this file describe only the environment your
28	service runs in (`HARNESS_API_DOTNET.md`) and the answer key you write (`TRUTH_SCHEMA_DOTNET.md`); neither one is a
29	design to imitate, and no example in them is a pattern to follow.
30	
31	## Where things go
32	
33	- OUT, as `HARNESS_API_DOTNET.md` uses the word, is this directory (`.`). SCRATCH is `./scratch`. Keep every build, log,
34	  package cache and helper script under `./scratch`.
35	- Hand back the service, its harness and `studio.toml` exactly as `HARNESS_API_DOTNET.md` lays them out, and a
36	  `truth.json` in the module directory written from your finished code exactly as `TRUTH_SCHEMA_DOTNET.md` lays it out,
37	  with a `file:line` for every fact.
38	- Run the checks of section 12 of `HARNESS_API_DOTNET.md` until every line reads `PASS` and the last reads
39	  `ALL CHECKS PASSED`.
40	- Then add three files to the module directory: `FILES.txt` (every file of the module, one path per line),
41	  `freeze.sha256` (the sha256 of every file named in `FILES.txt`), and `IDIOMS.md` with four lines saying, for your
42	  service: how a request reaches your code, how failures are answered, how sign-in and permission are decided, and where
43	  the database schema comes from.
44	
45	## Ground rules
46	
47	- Touch nothing outside this directory: do not read, list, search or write any path above it. Running the toolchain
48	  (`dotnet`, `python3`, ordinary shell utilities) is fine. No web browsing.
49	- Nobody will answer questions while you work; make each decision yourself.
50	- Your spending is capped. Get the service working first, then the answer key, then the three closing files.

SDK (10.0.401), and keep the data with EF Core in SQLite through the package `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite`.

## The product

Invent it. These subjects are taken and may not be used: habits, streaks, check-ins or reminders; tickets; runs; jobs;
notes; expenses, expense reports, reimbursements or payouts. Choose a subject that has real rules in it.

Whatever you invent must include all of the following:

- 10 to 16 HTTP routes in total, among them one where a person signs in with a name and a password;
- seeded people with at least two different roles, and at least one route that only one of those roles may use;
- at least two kinds of record that belong to the person who is signed in, so that no one can see or change somebody
  else's;
- at least one kind of record that belongs to a person only by way of a record it sits under;
- at least one stored value that the service keeps but never sends back in any answer;
- one record with a lifecycle: a state that changes at least twice over its life, where some changes are refused in
  some states;
- checking of what clients send, so that a request with a missing value or a value out of range is turned away.

## The code is yours

How the code is structured, and how each requirement above is met, are your decisions alone. Decide as you would for
a real product that is going to keep growing. The two documents beside this file describe only the environment your
service runs in (`HARNESS_API_DOTNET.md`) and the answer key you write (`TRUTH_SCHEMA_DOTNET.md`); neither one is a
design to imitate, and no example in them is a pattern to follow.

## Where things go

- OUT, as `HARNESS_API_DOTNET.md` uses the word, is this directory (`.`). SCRATCH is `./scratch`. Keep every build, log,
  package cache and helper script under `./scratch`.
- Hand back the service, its harness and `studio.toml` exactly as `HARNESS_API_DOTNET.md` lays them out, and a
  `truth.json` in the module directory written from your finished code exactly as `TRUTH_SCHEMA_DOTNET.md` lays it out,
  with a `file:line` for every fact.
- Run the checks of section 12 of `HARNESS_API_DOTNET.md` until every line reads `PASS` and the last reads
  `ALL CHECKS PASSED`.
- Then add three files to the module directory: `FILES.txt` (every file of the module, one path per line),
  `freeze.sha256` (the sha256 of every file named in `FILES.txt`), and `IDIOMS.md` with four lines saying, for your
  service: how a request reaches your code, how failures are answered, how sign-in and permission are decided, and where
  the database schema comes from.

## Ground rules

- Touch nothing outside this directory: do not read, list, search or write any path above it. Running the toolchain
  (`dotnet`, `python3`, ordinary shell utilities) is fine. No web browsing.
- Nobody will answer questions while you work; make each decision yourself.
- Your spending is capped. Get the service working first, then the answer key, then the three closing files.

1	# HARNESS_API_DOTNET: how your service is built, started, seeded, logged into and checked
2	
3	This file states every fact about the environment that will build, start and check your service. That environment is
4	not on your machine. Three Python names it provides (`AuthDriver` from `lattice.importer.transport`, `ProcessApp` and
5	`process_runtime` from `lattice.spec.process`, and `ServiceCmd` from `lattice.spec`) are imported by the harness file
6	you write; you cannot import them, so `smoke.py` (section 12) stands in for them with the same fields and the same
7	behaviour. Nothing here describes your service's design: that is yours.
8	
9	Replace `<x>` everywhere with the name you give the service: lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter. It
10	is also the name of the startup project and of its assembly.
11	
12	## 1. Layout of what you hand back
13	
14	Everything you hand back is under `OUT`, the directory your brief names:
15	
16	```
17	OUT/tests/spec/<x>/              the .NET project directory (the "module"): <x>.csproj (the startup project),
18	                                 packages.lock.json next to every project file, your sources, studio.toml, truth.json
19	OUT/tests/spec/<x>_harness.py    the harness (section 6)
20	```
21	
22	Create no other file under `OUT/tests/`; in particular create no `__init__.py` (section 11 says why none is needed).
23	The module directory holds no `bin/` and no `obj/` directory when you hand it back (a restore or a build run inside it
24	creates them: delete them, or build in a copy). Everything the build needs is inside the module directory: the
25	environment builds a copy of it, so a path that leaves it does not resolve. A project file compiles every `*.cs` file
26	below its own directory, including those of a project below it; keep each project's sources in a tree of their own.
27	If your startup project file is not `<x>.csproj` at the module root, change the `PROJECT` and `ASSEMBLY` constants of
28	the harness (section 6) and nothing else.
29	
30	## 2. Toolchain, packages and the build
31	
32	| fact | value |
33	|---|---|
34	| SDK | `dotnet --version` prints `10.0.401` (Homebrew, arm64). No global tool is installed (`dotnet tool list -g` is empty: no `dotnet-ef`), no workload is needed |
35	| runtimes | `Microsoft.NETCore.App 10.0.12` and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 10.0.12` only: no 8.0 or 9.0 runtime. Every project targets exactly `net10.0` |
36	| where packages come from | nuget.org (the machine's default and only source); the machine has network access to it; packages are cached in `~/.nuget/packages`. A `NuGet.config` in the module is not part of the contract |
37	| lock files | every project file sets `<RestorePackagesWithLockFile>true</RestorePackagesWithLockFile>`, and its `packages.lock.json` is committed next to it. Create it with `dotnet restore`; after changing a package reference refresh it with `dotnet restore --force-evaluate` |
38	| how it is built | `dotnet build <startup project> -c Release -p:RestoreLockedMode=true -o <output dir>` run on a copy of the module without `bin/` and `obj/`: it must succeed with 0 errors, restoring exactly the locked versions, and leave `packages.lock.json` byte-identical |
39	| a switch that does not exist | `dotnet build --locked-mode` is rejected by SDK 10.0.401 (`MSB1001: Unknown switch`); the property above is the form that works (`dotnet restore --locked-mode` is also valid). A missing `packages.lock.json` is NOT an error in that mode (restore writes one), so commit it |
40	| not allowed | a `NuGet.config` with other sources, a local package feed, binaries committed to the module, a restore that needs a global tool |
41	
42	Provider packages, each restored and run on this machine (net10.0, SDK 10.0.401):
43	
44	| use | package references | what they restore |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| EF Core over SQLite | `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite` 10.0.13 | EF Core 10.0.13, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite, SQLitePCLRaw 2.1.13; 0 warnings |
47	| MySQL, Pomelo | `Pomelo.EntityFrameworkCore.MySql` 9.0.0 (the newest; there is no EF Core 10 build) | `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` 9.0.0 and MySqlConnector 2.4.0. It requires `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Relational` `>= 9.0.0 && <= 9.0.999`: any EF Core 10 package in the same project fails the restore with `NU1107` |
48	| MySQL, Oracle | `MySql.EntityFrameworkCore` 10.0.9 (the EF Core 10 option) | `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` 10.0.9 and `MySql.Data` 26.7.0 |
49	| SQLite next to Pomelo | `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite` 9.0.0 or 9.0.21 (EF Core 9) | 9.0.0 prints warning `NU1903` (a known vulnerability in the native SQLitePCLRaw 2.1.10 library); 9.0.21 prints none. Both ran |
50	| SQLite next to Oracle | `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite` 10.0.9 or 10.0.13 | 10.0.9 prints `NU1903` (SQLitePCLRaw 2.1.11); 10.0.13 prints none. Both ran |
51	
52	A warning is not an error: nothing in the environment promotes warnings to errors. The lowest package version a restore
53	accepts is the one in the lock file; a higher version of a package that another package only lower-bounds is allowed
54	(Oracle's 10.0.9 ran on EF Core 10.0.13, Pomelo's 9.0.0 on EF Core 9.0.21).
55	
56	To keep every file the toolchain writes inside your scratch directory, export before any command (`SCRATCH` is the
57	scratch directory your brief names; a cold package cache downloads about 100 MB and works):
58	
59	```sh
60	export SCRATCH=<your scratch directory>
61	export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH
62	export DOTNET_ROOT=/opt/homebrew/opt/dotnet/libexec DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 DOTNET_NOLOGO=1
63	export HOME=$SCRATCH/home DOTNET_CLI_HOME=$SCRATCH/home NUGET_PACKAGES=$SCRATCH/home/.nuget/packages TMPDIR=$SCRATCH/.tmp
64	mkdir -p "$HOME" "$TMPDIR"
65	```

67	## 3. The process contract
68	
69	The harness builds the module (a copy, into the system temporary directory) and starts the built service as
70	`dotnet <output dir>/<ASSEMBLY>.dll` (a plain `dotnet <dll>`, not `dotnet run`: `launchSettings.json` is not read).
71	
72	| fact | value |
73	|---|---|
74	| command line | `dotnet <ASSEMBLY>.dll`, no argument. A background service of the same project is started with the arguments you choose (section 9) |
75	| working directory | the output directory of the build (a temporary directory): the content root is that directory, and the content files the build copies to its output are found there. It is NOT the module directory: read no relative path into the sources |
76	| environment | the caller's environment, plus `PORT` (a free TCP port, decimal), `DB_PATH` (the database as `db_env` carries it, section 4), plus what the harness adds with `ProcessApp.env` (the skeleton adds `DB_PROVIDER` and `DB_CONNECTION`, section 8). The service must start with only these set; any other setting it reads needs a default. No `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT`/`DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT` is set: the hosting environment is `Production` unless the caller's environment says otherwise. The caller's environment may also hold `ASPNETCORE_URLS` |
77	| listening | on `127.0.0.1` at the port in `PORT`, and nowhere else: `smoke.py` connects to the machine's other IPv4 address at that port and fails if the connection is accepted. ASP.NET Core does not read `PORT` by itself (with nothing configured a web service listens on `http://localhost:5000`), and a value of `ASPNETCORE_URLS` in the caller's environment is not the port to use: the service reads `PORT` |
78	| database | the one named by the environment (a SQLite file, or a MySQL URL, section 8). The file may not exist yet, may be empty, or may already hold your tables |
79	| schema | the service creates its own tables and indexes when it starts, on a missing or empty SQLite file or an empty MySQL database, and changes nothing on a database that already holds the same schema. Anything the service inserts at start-up is deleted by the environment before it seeds, so nothing may depend on a start-up row |
80	| health | `GET /health` answers `200` (any JSON body, no credentials) within 10 seconds of the start (the environment waits up to 15 s, `startup_timeout`; `smoke.py` fails above 10 s). It starts calling at once. A start measured on a small EF Core service: 0.3 to 0.4 s |
81	| one process per database, a new one per scenario | a check starts a fresh process on each scenario's own database and stops it afterwards, so in-memory state starts empty every time. The environment also sends several requests at one live process at the same time, on one database |
82	| files | the service writes only its database (and SQLite's own side files `-journal`, `-wal`, `-shm`) and a temporary directory. It writes nothing in the module directory, nothing in the home directory (a framework feature that persists a key ring under the home directory by default writes outside the allowed places; `smoke.py` runs the service with an empty home directory and fails if anything is written there), no log file |
83	| network | none besides the database: no outgoing call, no container. MySQL 8.4 throwaway containers come from Lattice (`lattice.spec.dbserver`); the service never starts one |
84	| standard output | discarded. Standard error is captured and shown if the start fails |
85	| durability | every write is committed to the database before the answer is sent: the environment opens SQLite files with its own connection right after an answer and reads what was committed |
86	| answers | JSON |
87	| stop | SIGTERM to the process group, SIGKILL after 5 seconds |
88	| request timeout | 30 seconds per request |
89	
90	## 4. `ProcessApp`: every field
91	
92	`make_app(db)` answers a `ProcessApp`, a handle on the command, not started. It is a dataclass of `lattice.spec.process`;
93	these are all its fields, in order.
94	
95	| field | type | default | meaning |
96	|---|---|---|---|
97	| `argv` | `Sequence[str]` | required | the command: `[dotnet, "<output dir>/<ASSEMBLY>.dll"]` |
98	| `db_path` | `Path \| str \| None` | `None` | the database: a SQLite path (made absolute) or a MySQL URL (unchanged); the process gets it in the variable named by `db_env` |
99	| `env` | `Mapping[str, str]` | `{}` | added to the process environment (the caller's, unless `inherit_env` is False) |
100	| `cwd` | `Path \| str \| None` | `None` | the working directory (`None`: the caller's); the skeleton sets the build output directory |
101	| `health_path` | `str` | `"/health"` | the route that answers 200 once the service serves |
102	| `startup_timeout` | `float` | `15.0` | seconds to wait for `health_path` |
103	| `port_env` | `str` | `"PORT"` | the variable carrying the port |
104	| `db_env` | `str` | `"DB_PATH"` | the variable carrying `db_path` |
105	| `host` | `str` | `"127.0.0.1"` | the address the environment connects to |
106	| `inherit_env` | `bool` | `True` | start from the caller's environment (`False`: only `env` plus the two variables) |
107	| `stop_timeout` | `float` | `5.0` | seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL |
108	| `request_timeout` | `float` | `30.0` | seconds per request |
109	| `ready` | `str` | `"http"` | how start-up is detected; leave the default (`GET health_path` answers 200) |
110	| `grpc_port_env` | `str \| None` | `None` | not used by an HTTP service; leave it |
111	| `protos` | `Sequence[str]` | `()` | not used; leave it |
112	| `proto_paths` | `Sequence[str]` | `()` | not used; leave it |
113	| `proto_root` | `Path \| str \| None` | `None` | not used; leave it |
114	
115	Runtime state, not constructor arguments (set by the environment, read-only for you): `grpc_port`, `port`, `pid`,
116	`returncode`, `timings` (and the private `_proc`, `_stderr`, `_lock`).
117	
118	The skeleton sets `argv`, `db_path`, `env`, `cwd` and `health_path`; set another field only if your brief says so.

120	## 5. The names the harness defines
121	
122	`OUT/tests/spec/<x>_harness.py` defines these names (names are exact):
123	
124	| name | what |
125	|---|---|
126	| `MODULE` | `Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "<x>"`, the module directory |
127	| `USERS` | `dict[str, tuple[str, str]]`: handle to (login name, password); at least two entries; the password is the text typed at login |
128	| `make_app(db) -> ProcessApp` | builds the service (once per change of the sources, into the temporary directory) and answers a `ProcessApp`. `db` is a `Path` (SQLite) or a `str` (a MySQL URL or, from the importer, a path). The return annotation `ProcessApp` is required |
129	| `build_db(db)` | creates and seeds the database at `db` and RETURNS `db`, the very argument; callers use the returned value, so a function that returns `None` fails |
130	| `RUNTIME` | `process_runtime(framework="dotnet", auth=AuthDriver.json(<login path>, USERS, ...))`, or, for a login that needs more than a name and a password, `process_runtime(framework="dotnet", auth=AuthDriver(login=login))` (section 7) |
131	| `LOGIN` | `RUNTIME.auth.login`, or your `login` function |
132	| `SERVICES` | `{service name: (db) -> ServiceCmd}` when the product has a background worker (section 9); `{}` otherwise |

231	    tmp = root / f"out-{os.getpid()}"

260	    and for MySql.EntityFrameworkCore 10.0.9 (Oracle's MySql.Data): both parse these keys and values."""
261	    p = urlsplit(url)

315	"""  # noqa: E501

334	    if is_url(db):

346	                             f'VALUES ({", ".join("?" for _ in cols)})', [_sqlite_value(row[c]) for c in cols])  # fmt: skip

356	    app = make_app(url)

373	## 7. Logging in
374	
375	`LOGIN(client, handle)` is called for each key of `USERS`; `client` is an `httpx.Client` on the service's base URL
376	(`client.post(path, json=...)`, `client.get(...)`; an answer has `.status_code`, `.text`, `.headers`, `.json()`). The
377	token it returns is an opaque string. Every later call of that user carries the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
378	
379	With `AuthDriver.json(path, USERS)`, `LOGIN` does `client.post(path, json={username_field: login_name, password_field:
380	password})`, requires status exactly `200`, reads the JSON answer, follows `token_path` (default: the key
381	`access_token` of the top-level object) and returns that string. So the login route is:
382	
383	- `POST <path>` (any path, passed as the first argument of `AuthDriver.json`);
384	- a JSON body with the two fields named by `username_field` and `password_field` (defaults `username` and `password`;
385	  pass others as keyword arguments);
386	- on success `200` with a JSON object holding the string at `token_path` (a tuple of keys, `("data", "token")` reads
387	  `answer["data"]["token"]`); a wrong login is refused with a 4xx.
388	
389	When the login needs another field (an installation id, say) or a different shape, write the function yourself and
390	use it for both names:
391	
392	```python
393	def login(client, handle: str) -> str:
394	    name, password = USERS[handle]
395	    r = client.post("/some/login", json={"email": name, "password": password, "installation_id": "..."})
396	    if r.status_code != 200:
397	        raise RuntimeError(f"login as {handle!r} failed: {r.status_code} {r.text[:200]}")
398	    return r.json()["access_token"]
399	
400	RUNTIME = process_runtime(framework="dotnet", auth=AuthDriver(login=login))
401	LOGIN = login
402	```
403	
404	Both forms were run through `python -m lattice.spec check` on a .NET service.

406	## 8. Databases, seed users and the stored password
407	
408	### 8.1 SQLite
409	
410	`make_app(db)` gets a `Path`. The skeleton puts it in the environment three ways: `DB_PATH` (the absolute path),
411	`DB_PROVIDER=sqlite` and `DB_CONNECTION=Data Source=<absolute path>` (the Microsoft.Data.Sqlite form). A service that
412	reads other names reads whatever its brief says; the environment sets only what `ProcessApp` says.
413	
414	### 8.2 MySQL 8.4 (when the brief makes it a database)
415	
416	The environment gives the harness a URL `mysql://root:lattice@127.0.0.1:<port>/<database>` of an empty database on a
417	throwaway `mysql:8.4` container of Lattice's (server 8.4.11, `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`, `lower_case_table_names = 0`: table
418	names are case-sensitive; the global `sql_mode` holds `STRICT_TRANS_TABLES`). What happens, in order:
419	
420	1. `build_db(url)` runs ONCE per seed on an empty database. It has the service create its schema (the skeleton
421	   starts the service once on the empty database and stops it), then inserts the seed rows through Lattice's adapter
422	   (`lattice.spec.db.open_db(url).insert(table, rows)`).
423	2. Every scenario and every concurrency check runs on a CLONE of that database: `CREATE DATABASE`, then each table's
424	   `SHOW CREATE TABLE` replayed (indexes, generated columns, CHECK and foreign keys kept) and its rows copied with
425	   foreign key checks off, then views and triggers; the clone is dropped afterwards. So the schema must be
426	   reproducible by `SHOW CREATE TABLE` (tables, views, triggers), and tables the service keeps for itself are cloned too.
427	3. `make_app(clone_url)` and the services get the clone's URL. The service is started on it.
428	
429	The checker reads and writes the database directly, with the table and column names of the spec (given rows,
430	`expect_db`, invariants): the names in the database are the spec's names, spelled as the spec spells them.
431	
432	The URL as an ADO.NET connection string: `adonet_mysql(url)` of the skeleton. The one form below was run against
433	`Pomelo.EntityFrameworkCore.MySql` 9.0.0 (MySqlConnector) and `MySql.EntityFrameworkCore` 10.0.9 (Oracle, MySql.Data),
434	each creating its schema and reading and writing rows on the 8.4 container:
435	
436	```
437	Server=127.0.0.1;Port=<port>;Database=<database>;User ID=root;Password=lattice;SslMode=Disabled;AllowPublicKeyRetrieval=True
438	```
439	
440	`Uid` and `Pwd` for `User ID` and `Password` are accepted by both. `SslMode=None` is accepted by Pomelo but rejected by
441	the Oracle provider (`ArgumentException: Requested value 'None' was not found`): use `Disabled`. A password that holds
442	`;`, `"`, `'`, `=` or spaces is double-quoted with `""` for a quote (the skeleton does it; `smoke.py` checks the round trip
443	through a reader of that syntax, and both providers' string builders read the same values back).
444	
445	Instants in the spec's `given` rows are written as `"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"`. A strict MySQL session refuses the trailing `Z`
446	(`1292 Incorrect datetime value`, verified); the harness therefore drops `STRICT_TRANS_TABLES` from the **global**
447	`sql_mode` of Lattice's own throwaway server (user `root`, password `lattice`, host `127.0.0.1`) when it seeds
448	(`CHECKER_SQL_MODE` in the skeleton). That affects only the checker's connections: a service that wants a strict mode sets
449	it on its own session.
450	
451	### 8.3 Seed users and the stored password
452	
453	Two kinds of seeded database exist.
454	
455	**Yours (`build_db`).** The users of `USERS` (at least two), each with its login name and its password stored EXACTLY as
456	typed at login in the users table: the login must succeed for a row whose password column holds that plain text, and
457	the answers never carry it. `seed_rows()` is where the rows are written; they must satisfy the route check of section 10.
458	On SQLite `build_db` writes the schema by hand in plain SQL (the `DDL` string), identical to what the service itself
459	creates on an empty file (`python3 smoke.py OUT <x> schema` prints it), then the rows.
460	
461	**The checking environment's own** (used when the service has a SQLite provider). It starts your
462	service on an empty SQLite file once, lets it create its schema, deletes every row the service wrote at start-up, then
463	inserts rows itself by plain SQL, without calling the service, and then logs in through your login route. The users it
464	writes are `admin`, `alice`, `bob` and `carol`; the login name is `<handle>@example.com` (for example
465	`alice@example.com`, so the login-name column must accept at least 40 characters), the password is `<handle>-pass-0031`
466	(for example `alice-pass-0031`), and the password column holds that text exactly as typed, as for yours. A second
467	database for a re-probe uses `-pass-0097`, other row counts and other integer keys: depend on no id. Every other column
468	gets a placeholder (text such as `Name 01`, integers, 0/1 for booleans, timestamps as text `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff`
469	in UTC, foreign keys pointing at rows it inserted), respecting NOT NULL and uniqueness. The users table has a text column
470	that holds the login name, named like the login body's username field or the first unique text column of the table.
471	
472	## 9. Background services
473	
474	When the spec names a background service, `SERVICES[name](db)` answers a `ServiceCmd(argv, env, cwd, stop_timeout)`:
475	how that service starts on the scenario's database (`db` is a SQLite path, or the clone's URL on MySQL). An `Await` step
476	of a scenario starts it on that scenario's database, polls the database about every 0.2 s until the step's `expect_db`
477	holds (within the step's seconds it passes, else a finding), and stops it (its process group: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL
478	after `stop_timeout`) whatever happened. The service runs with the caller's environment plus `ServiceCmd.env`; it gets
479	no `PORT`. It is a separate process: the skeleton starts the same built assembly with the argument `worker`; how your
480	program reacts to an argument is yours. The service's database access must commit each change (the checker reads the
481	database from outside). `smoke.py` starts every `SERVICES` entry on the seeded SQLite file for 2 seconds and fails if it
482	exits with an error.
483	
484	## 10. The route check, and `truth.json`
485	
486	For every route of `truth.json` the environment makes one call:
487	
488	- every `{...}` segment of the route's `template` is replaced by `1`: path parameters are integer row ids;
489	- a `POST`, `PUT` or `PATCH` carries the JSON body `{}`;
490	- the caller is the first user of `USERS` whose role in `truth.json` `seed_users` matches the route's `auth` (`Member`
491	  or `Admin`); a `Public` route is called without credentials;
492	- order: all `GET`s, then the writes, then the `DELETE`s.
493	
494	The status must be neither `404` nor `405`, which is what an unregistered route answers. A `404` that your own code
495	answers for a missing row is not told apart from it. So `build_db` must seed, for each table a path parameter names, a row
496	with id `1` that the calling user may reach (it belongs to that user, directly or through its parents), and the parent
497	rows it needs. The environment also calls each non-public route without credentials and expects `401` or `403` (a
498	warning, not a failure). If your brief fixes the rows of the seed, `build_db` writes exactly those and no more; a
499	path-parameter route then may answer `404` for the missing row, and `python3 smoke.py OUT <x> --warn-404` prints it as a
500	warning instead of a failure.
501	
502	`smoke.py` reads only these keys of `truth.json` (its full schema is in your brief): `routes[{method, template, auth,
503	file, line}]`, `seed_users[{name, role}]` (one per login name of `USERS`, roles `Member` or `Admin`) and `login.path`
504	(a public `POST` route in `routes`).
505	
506	## 11. `studio.toml`, and how the harness module is imported
507	
508	```toml
509	[app]
510	app = "tests.spec.<x>_harness:make_app"
511	db = "tests.spec.<x>_harness:build_db"
512	runtime = "tests.spec.<x>_harness:RUNTIME"
513	```
514	
515	Keys of the table `[app]` that Lattice reads: `app`, `db`, `runtime` (always), and `login`
516	(`"tests.spec.<x>_harness:LOGIN"`, when a function other than the runtime's is the login), `services`
517	(`"tests.spec.<x>_harness:SERVICES"`, when there are background services), `database` (`"mysql"` or `"sqlite"`; absent:
518	`sqlite`), `login_path`, `database_url`. Use only the keys your brief asks for.
519	
520	The DOTTED module form `tests.spec.<x>_harness:<attribute>` is required. The bare form `<x>_harness:make_app` cannot be
521	imported by the environment (it answers `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '<x>_harness'`; checked). The dotted form
522	resolves because the environment runs from the repository root, which is on `sys.path`: `tests/` has NO `__init__.py`
523	(a namespace package) and `tests/spec/` has one (an empty file, already in the repository). So create neither.
524	
525	The harness runs inside Lattice's Python process: `lattice` is importable there, and so are `httpx` and, for MySQL,
526	PyMySQL. Import only the standard library and those names; the harness prints nothing on import.

528	## 12. Check it yourself without the checking environment
529	
530	Save the script below as `$SCRATCH/smoke.py` (outside `OUT`) and run it, after the exports of section 2, with Python 3.11+
531	and nothing installed:
532	
533	```sh
534	python3 $SCRATCH/smoke.py $OUT <x> schema        # starts the service on an empty SQLite file, prints the schema it creates
535	python3 $SCRATCH/smoke.py $OUT <x>               # every check
536	python3 $SCRATCH/smoke.py $OUT <x> --warn-404    # as above, a 404 on a path-parameter route is a warning
537	```
538	
539	Use the output of the first command as the `DDL` of the harness. The second command runs, in this order: the layout (the
540	files exist, no `bin/` or `obj/`); `studio.toml` (dotted keys); `dotnet --version` is 10.0.401; every project file targets
541	`net10.0`, sets `RestorePackagesWithLockFile` and has a `packages.lock.json`; the clean-copy build with
542	`-p:RestoreLockedMode=true` (it stops here if the build fails) and the lock file unchanged by it; the harness (names,
543	`USERS`, `RUNTIME.framework`, `adonet_mysql` round trips, `build_db` returns its argument and is repeatable, the stored
544	plain passwords); `make_app` and the start on the seeded file (`GET /health` is 200 within 10 s, the tables, columns and
545	indexes unchanged by the start, the listener refuses the machine's other address); the login of every seed user; the
546	`truth.json` keys and the route check of section 10; the stop; every `SERVICES` entry for 2 seconds; the start on a missing
547	file and the equality of the schema it creates with the schema `build_db` writes; that the service wrote nothing to its
548	home directory, nothing but SQLite's side files next to its database, and nothing in the module. All lines must read

642	def http(method: str, url: str, token: str | None = None, body: Any = None, timeout: float = 30.0,
643	         headers: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> Resp:
644	    data = None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode()

646	    if data is not None:

650	    for k, v in (headers or {}).items():
651	        req.add_header(k, v)
652	    try:
653	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
654	            return Resp(r.status, r.read().decode(errors="replace"), dict(r.headers))
655	    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
656	        return Resp(e.code, e.read().decode(errors="replace"), dict(e.headers))

745	        self.proc = subprocess.Popen([str(x) for x in a.argv], cwd=None if a.cwd is None else str(a.cwd), env=env,
746	                                     stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=self.err,
747	                                     start_new_session=True)
748	        base = f"http://{a.host}:{self.port}"

750	        while True:

752	                raise RuntimeError(f"exited with code {self.proc.returncode} before answering {a.health_path}; "
753	                                   f"stderr:\n{self.stderr()}")
754	            try:
755	                if http("GET", base + a.health_path, timeout=1.0).status_code == 200:
756	                    self.health_s = time.monotonic() - t0
757	                    return base
758	            except OSError:
759	                pass
760	            if time.monotonic() > deadline:
761	                raise RuntimeError(f"no 200 on {a.health_path} within {a.startup_timeout:g}s; stderr:\n{self.stderr()}")

790	def snapshot(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
791	    """Tables (column name, type, not null, primary key) and indexes (unique, columns) of a SQLite file."""
792	    con = sqlite3.connect(path)
793	    try:
794	        out: dict[str, Any] = {}
795	        tables = [r[0] for r in con.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' "
796	                                            "AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' ORDER BY name")]
797	        for t in tables:
798	            cols = sorted((c[1], c[2].lower(), c[3], c[5]) for c in con.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{t}")'))
799	            idx = sorted((i[2], tuple(x[2] for x in con.execute(f'PRAGMA index_info("{i[1]}")')))
800	                         for i in con.execute(f'PRAGMA index_list("{t}")') if not i[1].startswith("sqlite_"))
801	            out[t] = {"columns": cols, "indexes": idx}
802	        return out
803	    finally:
804	        con.close()

812	def file_line_ok(module: Path, ref: Any) -> bool:
813	    if not isinstance(ref, str) or ":" not in ref:
814	        return False
815	    name, _, line = ref.rpartition(":")
816	    p = (module / name).resolve()

822	def parse_adonet(s: str) -> dict[str, str]:
823	    """A small ADO.NET connection-string reader (keys case-folded, double-quoted values with "" for a quote)."""
824	    out: dict[str, str] = {}
825	    i = 0
826	    while i < len(s):
827	        eq = s.index("=", i)
828	        key = s[i:eq].strip().lower()
829	        i = eq + 1
830	        if i < len(s) and s[i] == '"':
831	            i += 1
832	            val = ""
833	            while True:
834	                if s[i] == '"' and i + 1 < len(s) and s[i + 1] == '"':
835	                    val += '"'
836	                    i += 2
837	                elif s[i] == '"':
838	                    i += 1
839	                    break
840	                else:
841	                    val += s[i]
842	                    i += 1
843	            while i < len(s) and s[i] != ";":
844	                i += 1
845	        else:
846	            j = s.find(";", i)
847	            j = len(s) if j < 0 else j
848	            val = s[i:j]
849	            i = j
850	        out[key] = val
851	        i += 1
852	    return out

891	def sweep(truth: dict[str, Any], base: str, users: dict[str, Any], tokens: dict[str, str]) -> None:
892	    """Every truth route, called as a user who may call it, path parameters replaced by 1, {} on writes."""
893	    roles = {u["name"]: u["role"] for u in truth.get("seed_users", [])}
894	    by_role: dict[str, str] = {}
895	    for handle, (login_name, _pw) in users.items():
896	        role = roles.get(login_name)
897	        if role and handle in tokens:
898	            by_role.setdefault(role, tokens[handle])
899	    order = {"GET": 0, "POST": 1, "PUT": 1, "PATCH": 1, "DELETE": 2}

# HARNESS_API_DOTNET: how your service is built, started, seeded, logged into and checked

This file states every fact about the environment that will build, start and check your service. That environment is
not on your machine. Three Python names it provides (`AuthDriver` from `lattice.importer.transport`, `ProcessApp` and
`process_runtime` from `lattice.spec.process`, and `ServiceCmd` from `lattice.spec`) are imported by the harness file
you write; you cannot import them, so `smoke.py` (section 12) stands in for them with the same fields and the same
behaviour. Nothing here describes your service's design: that is yours.

Replace `<x>` everywhere with the name you give the service: lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter. It
is also the name of the startup project and of its assembly.

## 1. Layout of what you hand back

Everything you hand back is under `OUT`, the directory your brief names:

```
OUT/tests/spec/<x>/              the .NET project directory (the "module"): <x>.csproj (the startup project),
                                 packages.lock.json next to every project file, your sources, studio.toml, truth.json
OUT/tests/spec/<x>_harness.py    the harness (section 6)
```

Create no other file under `OUT/tests/`; in particular create no `__init__.py` (section 11 says why none is needed).
The module directory holds no `bin/` and no `obj/` directory when you hand it back (a restore or a build run inside it
creates them: delete them, or build in a copy). Everything the build needs is inside the module directory: the
environment builds a copy of it, so a path that leaves it does not resolve. A project file compiles every `*.cs` file
below its own directory, including those of a project below it; keep each project's sources in a tree of their own.
If your startup project file is not `<x>.csproj` at the module root, change the `PROJECT` and `ASSEMBLY` constants of
the harness (section 6) and nothing else.

## 2. Toolchain, packages and the build

| fact | value |
|---|---|
| SDK | `dotnet --version` prints `10.0.401` (Homebrew, arm64). No global tool is installed (`dotnet tool list -g` is empty: no `dotnet-ef`), no workload is needed |
| runtimes | `Microsoft.NETCore.App 10.0.12` and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 10.0.12` only: no 8.0 or 9.0 runtime. Every project targets exactly `net10.0` |
| where packages come from | nuget.org (the machine's default and only source); the machine has network access to it; packages are cached in `~/.nuget/packages`. A `NuGet.config` in the module is not part of the contract |
| lock files | every project file sets `<RestorePackagesWithLockFile>true</RestorePackagesWithLockFile>`, and its `packages.lock.json` is committed next to it. Create it with `dotnet restore`; after changing a package reference refresh it with `dotnet restore --force-evaluate` |
| how it is built | `dotnet build <startup project> -c Release -p:RestoreLockedMode=true -o <output dir>` run on a copy of the module without `bin/` and `obj/`: it must succeed with 0 errors, restoring exactly the locked versions, and leave `packages.lock.json` byte-identical |
| a switch that does not exist | `dotnet build --locked-mode` is rejected by SDK 10.0.401 (`MSB1001: Unknown switch`); the property above is the form that works (`dotnet restore --locked-mode` is also valid). A missing `packages.lock.json` is NOT an error in that mode (restore writes one), so commit it |
| not allowed | a `NuGet.config` with other sources, a local package feed, binaries committed to the module, a restore that needs a global tool |

Provider packages, each restored and run on this machine (net10.0, SDK 10.0.401):

| use | package references | what they restore |
|---|---|---|
| EF Core over SQLite | `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite` 10.0.13 | EF Core 10.0.13, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite, SQLitePCLRaw 2.1.13; 0 warnings |
| MySQL, Pomelo | `Pomelo.EntityFrameworkCore.MySql` 9.0.0 (the newest; there is no EF Core 10 build) | `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` 9.0.0 and MySqlConnector 2.4.0. It requires `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Relational` `>= 9.0.0 && <= 9.0.999`: any EF Core 10 package in the same project fails the restore with `NU1107` |
| MySQL, Oracle | `MySql.EntityFrameworkCore` 10.0.9 (the EF Core 10 option) | `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` 10.0.9 and `MySql.Data` 26.7.0 |
| SQLite next to Pomelo | `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite` 9.0.0 or 9.0.21 (EF Core 9) | 9.0.0 prints warning `NU1903` (a known vulnerability in the native SQLitePCLRaw 2.1.10 library); 9.0.21 prints none. Both ran |
| SQLite next to Oracle | `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite` 10.0.9 or 10.0.13 | 10.0.9 prints `NU1903` (SQLitePCLRaw 2.1.11); 10.0.13 prints none. Both ran |

A warning is not an error: nothing in the environment promotes warnings to errors. The lowest package version a restore
accepts is the one in the lock file; a higher version of a package that another package only lower-bounds is allowed
(Oracle's 10.0.9 ran on EF Core 10.0.13, Pomelo's 9.0.0 on EF Core 9.0.21).

To keep every file the toolchain writes inside your scratch directory, export before any command (`SCRATCH` is the
scratch directory your brief names; a cold package cache downloads about 100 MB and works):

```sh
export SCRATCH=<your scratch directory>
export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH
export DOTNET_ROOT=/opt/homebrew/opt/dotnet/libexec DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 DOTNET_NOLOGO=1
export HOME=$SCRATCH/home DOTNET_CLI_HOME=$SCRATCH/home NUGET_PACKAGES=$SCRATCH/home/.nuget/packages TMPDIR=$SCRATCH/.tmp
mkdir -p "$HOME" "$TMPDIR"
```

## 3. The process contract

The harness builds the module (a copy, into the system temporary directory) and starts the built service as
`dotnet <output dir>/<ASSEMBLY>.dll` (a plain `dotnet <dll>`, not `dotnet run`: `launchSettings.json` is not read).

| fact | value |
|---|---|
| command line | `dotnet <ASSEMBLY>.dll`, no argument. A background service of the same project is started with the arguments you choose (section 9) |
| working directory | the output directory of the build (a temporary directory): the content root is that directory, and the content files the build copies to its output are found there. It is NOT the module directory: read no relative path into the sources |
| environment | the caller's environment, plus `PORT` (a free TCP port, decimal), `DB_PATH` (the database as `db_env` carries it, section 4), plus what the harness adds with `ProcessApp.env` (the skeleton adds `DB_PROVIDER` and `DB_CONNECTION`, section 8). The service must start with only these set; any other setting it reads needs a default. No `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT`/`DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT` is set: the hosting environment is `Production` unless the caller's environment says otherwise. The caller's environment may also hold `ASPNETCORE_URLS` |
| listening | on `127.0.0.1` at the port in `PORT`, and nowhere else: `smoke.py` connects to the machine's other IPv4 address at that port and fails if the connection is accepted. ASP.NET Core does not read `PORT` by itself (with nothing configured a web service listens on `http://localhost:5000`), and a value of `ASPNETCORE_URLS` in the caller's environment is not the port to use: the service reads `PORT` |
| database | the one named by the environment (a SQLite file, or a MySQL URL, section 8). The file may not exist yet, may be empty, or may already hold your tables |
| schema | the service creates its own tables and indexes when it starts, on a missing or empty SQLite file or an empty MySQL database, and changes nothing on a database that already holds the same schema. Anything the service inserts at start-up is deleted by the environment before it seeds, so nothing may depend on a start-up row |
| health | `GET /health` answers `200` (any JSON body, no credentials) within 10 seconds of the start (the environment waits up to 15 s, `startup_timeout`; `smoke.py` fails above 10 s). It starts calling at once. A start measured on a small EF Core service: 0.3 to 0.4 s |
| one process per database, a new one per scenario | a check starts a fresh process on each scenario's own database and stops it afterwards, so in-memory state starts empty every time. The environment also sends several requests at one live process at the same time, on one database |
| files | the service writes only its database (and SQLite's own side files `-journal`, `-wal`, `-shm`) and a temporary directory. It writes nothing in the module directory, nothing in the home directory (a framework feature that persists a key ring under the home directory by default writes outside the allowed places; `smoke.py` runs the service with an empty home directory and fails if anything is written there), no log file |
| network | none besides the database: no outgoing call, no container. MySQL 8.4 throwaway containers come from Lattice (`lattice.spec.dbserver`); the service never starts one |
| standard output | discarded. Standard error is captured and shown if the start fails |
| durability | every write is committed to the database before the answer is sent: the environment opens SQLite files with its own connection right after an answer and reads what was committed |
| answers | JSON |
| stop | SIGTERM to the process group, SIGKILL after 5 seconds |
| request timeout | 30 seconds per request |

## 4. `ProcessApp`: every field

`make_app(db)` answers a `ProcessApp`, a handle on the command, not started. It is a dataclass of `lattice.spec.process`;
these are all its fields, in order.

| field | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `argv` | `Sequence[str]` | required | the command: `[dotnet, "<output dir>/<ASSEMBLY>.dll"]` |
| `db_path` | `Path \| str \| None` | `None` | the database: a SQLite path (made absolute) or a MySQL URL (unchanged); the process gets it in the variable named by `db_env` |
| `env` | `Mapping[str, str]` | `{}` | added to the process environment (the caller's, unless `inherit_env` is False) |
| `cwd` | `Path \| str \| None` | `None` | the working directory (`None`: the caller's); the skeleton sets the build output directory |
| `health_path` | `str` | `"/health"` | the route that answers 200 once the service serves |

```python
"""Harness of tests/spec/<NAME>: how the service is built and started, how its database is seeded, how callers log in.

``make_app(db)`` answers a ProcessApp (the command, not started). The service is built once per change of its sources,
from a copy of the module directory, into the system temp directory; the module directory is never written.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import os
import shutil
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import tempfile
import zlib
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit

from lattice.importer.transport import AuthDriver
from lattice.spec import ServiceCmd
from lattice.spec.process import ProcessApp, process_runtime

MODULE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "<NAME>"
PROJECT = "<NAME>.csproj"  # the startup project, relative to MODULE
ASSEMBLY = "<NAME>"  # its assembly name: the build writes <ASSEMBLY>.dll
BUILD_ENV = "<NAME>_OUT"  # optional: a directory holding an already built <ASSEMBLY>.dll, instead of building
# handle -> (login name, password); at least two entries; the password is the one typed at login
USERS = {"ann": ("ann", "pw-ann"), "ben": ("ben", "pw-ben")}
BUILD_TIMEOUT_S = 900


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- build and start


def _source_key() -> str:
    """A short key of the module's sources: the build is redone only when they change."""
    crc = 0
    for p in sorted(MODULE.rglob("*")):
        rel = p.relative_to(MODULE)
        if p.is_file() and not {"bin", "obj"} & set(rel.parts):
            crc = zlib.crc32(rel.as_posix().encode() + b"\0" + p.read_bytes() + b"\0", crc)
    return f"{crc:08x}"


def _dotnet() -> str:
    found = shutil.which("dotnet")
    if found is None:
        raise RuntimeError("<NAME>: `dotnet` is not on PATH")
    return found


def build_dir() -> Path:
    """The directory holding the built service: ``$<NAME>_OUT``, else built (once per source key) into the system
    temp directory from a copy of MODULE (bin and obj left out)."""
    if env := os.environ.get(BUILD_ENV):
        return Path(env)
    root = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"build-<NAME>-{_source_key()}"
    out = root / "out"
    if (out / f"{ASSEMBLY}.dll").is_file():
        return out
    shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)
    src = root / "src"
    shutil.copytree(MODULE, src, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("bin", "obj"))
    env = {**os.environ, "DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT": "1", "DOTNET_NOLOGO": "1"}
    tmp = root / f"out-{os.getpid()}"
    proc = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 -- the module's own build
        [_dotnet(), "build", str(src / PROJECT), "-c", "Release", "-p:RestoreLockedMode=true", "-o", str(tmp), "--nologo"],
        cwd=src, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, env=env, timeout=BUILD_TIMEOUT_S,
    )  # fmt: skip
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)
        raise RuntimeError(f"<NAME>: dotnet build failed:\n{(proc.stdout + proc.stderr).strip()[-3000:]}")
    os.replace(tmp, out)
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- database references


def is_url(db: object) -> bool:
    """A server database is a URL (``mysql://user:password@host:port/name``), a SQLite database a file path."""
    return "://" in str(db)


def _value(v: str) -> str:
    """One ADO.NET connection-string value, quoted when it holds a character the syntax reserves."""
    if v == "" or any(c in v for c in ";\"'=") or v != v.strip():
        return '"' + v.replace('"', '""') + '"'
    return v


def adonet_mysql(url: str) -> str:
    """The ADO.NET connection string of a ``mysql://`` URL, for Pomelo.EntityFrameworkCore.MySql 9.0.0 (MySqlConnector)
    and for MySql.EntityFrameworkCore 10.0.9 (Oracle's MySql.Data): both parse these keys and values."""
    p = urlsplit(url)
    parts = [("Server", p.hostname or "127.0.0.1"), ("Port", str(p.port or 3306)), ("Database", unquote(p.path.lstrip("/"))),
             ("User ID", unquote(p.username or "")), ("Password", unquote(p.password or "")),
             ("SslMode", "Disabled"), ("AllowPublicKeyRetrieval", "True")]  # fmt: skip
    return ";".join(f"{k}={_value(v)}" for k, v in parts)


def adonet_sqlite(path: str | Path) -> str:
    """The Microsoft.Data.Sqlite connection string of a database file."""
    return f"Data Source={Path(path).resolve()}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the app and its services


def make_app(db: Path | str) -> ProcessApp:
    """The service on ``db`` (a SQLite path, or a MySQL URL). The service creates its own schema when it starts on an
    empty database. It receives PORT, DB_PATH (``db`` as given, a path made absolute), DB_PROVIDER (``sqlite`` or
    ``mysql``) and DB_CONNECTION (the ADO.NET string)."""
    out = build_dir()
    server = is_url(db)
    env = {"DB_PROVIDER": "mysql" if server else "sqlite",
           "DB_CONNECTION": adonet_mysql(str(db)) if server else adonet_sqlite(db)}  # fmt: skip
    return ProcessApp([_dotnet(), str(out / f"{ASSEMBLY}.dll")], db_path=db, env=env, cwd=str(out), health_path="/health")


def _worker(db: Path | str) -> ServiceCmd:
    """TODO (only when the spec names a background service): how the service starts on ``db``."""
    app = make_app(db)
    return ServiceCmd([*app.argv, "worker"], env={**app.env, "DB_PATH": str(db)}, cwd=app.cwd)


# the spec's background services {name: (db) -> ServiceCmd}; empty when the product has none
SERVICES: dict = {}  # TODO e.g. {"worker": _worker}

RUNTIME = process_runtime(framework="dotnet", auth=AuthDriver.json("/login", USERS))
LOGIN = RUNTIME.auth.login


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the seed


def seed_rows() -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
    """The seed: table -> rows (column -> value; str, int, float, bool, None or datetime), parents before children.
    The users of USERS carry id 1, 2, ... and their plain password in the password column."""
    users = []
    for i, (login_name, password) in enumerate(USERS.values(), 1):
        users.append({})  # TODO: the user's columns: id i, the login name, the plain password, and every NOT NULL column
    return {"users": users}  # TODO: the other seed rows, one list per table


# The schema exactly as the service creates it on an empty SQLite file (``python3 smoke.py OUT <NAME> schema`` prints it).
DDL = """
-- TODO: the CREATE TABLE / CREATE INDEX statements, one per table and index, each ending with a semicolon
"""  # noqa: E501

# MySQL only: the session mode of the checker's own connections, without STRICT_TRANS_TABLES (see HARNESS_API_DOTNET.md)
CHECKER_SQL_MODE = ("ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,NO_ZERO_DATE,"
                    "ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION")  # fmt: skip


def _sqlite_value(v: object) -> object:
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return int(v)
    if isinstance(v, dt.datetime):
        return v.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f")
    return v


def build_db(db: Path | str) -> Path | str:
    """A seeded database. A SQLite path: replaced, schema by hand (DDL), then the rows. A MySQL URL (an empty
    database): the service starts once and creates its schema, then the rows go in through Lattice's adapter.
    Answers ``db``, the very argument."""
    if is_url(db):
        return _build_server_db(str(db))
    path = Path(db)
    if path.exists():
        path.unlink()
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    try:
        conn.executescript(DDL)
        for table, rows in seed_rows().items():
            for row in rows:
                cols = list(row)
                conn.execute(f'INSERT INTO "{table}" ({", ".join(chr(34) + c + chr(34) for c in cols)}) '
                             f'VALUES ({", ".join("?" for _ in cols)})', [_sqlite_value(row[c]) for c in cols])  # fmt: skip
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()
    return db


def _build_server_db(url: str) -> str:
    from lattice.spec.db import UrlParts, open_db

    app = make_app(url)
    try:
        app.start()  # the service creates its schema on the empty database
    finally:
        app.stop()
    conn = open_db(url)
    try:
        u = UrlParts(url)
        if (u.host, u.user, u.password) == ("127.0.0.1", "root", "lattice"):  # Lattice's own throwaway server
            conn.execute(f"SET GLOBAL sql_mode = '{CHECKER_SQL_MODE}'")
        for table, rows in seed_rows().items():
            conn.insert(table, rows)
    finally:
        conn.close()
    return url
```

## 7. Logging in

`LOGIN(client, handle)` is called for each key of `USERS`; `client` is an `httpx.Client` on the service's base URL
(`client.post(path, json=...)`, `client.get(...)`; an answer has `.status_code`, `.text`, `.headers`, `.json()`). The
token it returns is an opaque string. Every later call of that user carries the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

With `AuthDriver.json(path, USERS)`, `LOGIN` does `client.post(path, json={username_field: login_name, password_field:
password})`, requires status exactly `200`, reads the JSON answer, follows `token_path` (default: the key
`access_token` of the top-level object) and returns that string. So the login route is:

- `POST <path>` (any path, passed as the first argument of `AuthDriver.json`);
- a JSON body with the two fields named by `username_field` and `password_field` (defaults `username` and `password`;
  pass others as keyword arguments);
- on success `200` with a JSON object holding the string at `token_path` (a tuple of keys, `("data", "token")` reads
  `answer["data"]["token"]`); a wrong login is refused with a 4xx.

When the login needs another field (an installation id, say) or a different shape, write the function yourself and
use it for both names:

```python
def login(client, handle: str) -> str:
    name, password = USERS[handle]
    r = client.post("/some/login", json={"email": name, "password": password, "installation_id": "..."})
    if r.status_code != 200:
        raise RuntimeError(f"login as {handle!r} failed: {r.status_code} {r.text[:200]}")
    return r.json()["access_token"]

RUNTIME = process_runtime(framework="dotnet", auth=AuthDriver(login=login))
LOGIN = login
```

Both forms were run through `python -m lattice.spec check` on a .NET service.

## 8. Databases, seed users and the stored password

### 8.1 SQLite

`make_app(db)` gets a `Path`. The skeleton puts it in the environment three ways: `DB_PATH` (the absolute path),
`DB_PROVIDER=sqlite` and `DB_CONNECTION=Data Source=<absolute path>` (the Microsoft.Data.Sqlite form). A service that
reads other names reads whatever its brief says; the environment sets only what `ProcessApp` says.

### 8.2 MySQL 8.4 (when the brief makes it a database)

The environment gives the harness a URL `mysql://root:lattice@127.0.0.1:<port>/<database>` of an empty database on a
throwaway `mysql:8.4` container of Lattice's (server 8.4.11, `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`, `lower_case_table_names = 0`: table
names are case-sensitive; the global `sql_mode` holds `STRICT_TRANS_TABLES`). What happens, in order:

1. `build_db(url)` runs ONCE per seed on an empty database. It has the service create its schema (the skeleton
   starts the service once on the empty database and stops it), then inserts the seed rows through Lattice's adapter
   (`lattice.spec.db.open_db(url).insert(table, rows)`).
2. Every scenario and every concurrency check runs on a CLONE of that database: `CREATE DATABASE`, then each table's
   `SHOW CREATE TABLE` replayed (indexes, generated columns, CHECK and foreign keys kept) and its rows copied with
   foreign key checks off, then views and triggers; the clone is dropped afterwards. So the schema must be
   reproducible by `SHOW CREATE TABLE` (tables, views, triggers), and tables the service keeps for itself are cloned too.
3. `make_app(clone_url)` and the services get the clone's URL. The service is started on it.

The checker reads and writes the database directly, with the table and column names of the spec (given rows,
`expect_db`, invariants): the names in the database are the spec's names, spelled as the spec spells them.

The URL as an ADO.NET connection string: `adonet_mysql(url)` of the skeleton. The one form below was run against
`Pomelo.EntityFrameworkCore.MySql` 9.0.0 (MySqlConnector) and `MySql.EntityFrameworkCore` 10.0.9 (Oracle, MySql.Data),
each creating its schema and reading and writing rows on the 8.4 container:

```
Server=127.0.0.1;Port=<port>;Database=<database>;User ID=root;Password=lattice;SslMode=Disabled;AllowPublicKeyRetrieval=True
```

`Uid` and `Pwd` for `User ID` and `Password` are accepted by both. `SslMode=None` is accepted by Pomelo but rejected by
the Oracle provider (`ArgumentException: Requested value 'None' was not found`): use `Disabled`. A password that holds
`;`, `"`, `'`, `=` or spaces is double-quoted with `""` for a quote (the skeleton does it; `smoke.py` checks the round trip
through a reader of that syntax, and both providers' string builders read the same values back).

Instants in the spec's `given` rows are written as `"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"`. A strict MySQL session refuses the trailing `Z`
(`1292 Incorrect datetime value`, verified); the harness therefore drops `STRICT_TRANS_TABLES` from the **global**
`sql_mode` of Lattice's own throwaway server (user `root`, password `lattice`, host `127.0.0.1`) when it seeds
(`CHECKER_SQL_MODE` in the skeleton). That affects only the checker's connections: a service that wants a strict mode sets
it on its own session.

### 8.3 Seed users and the stored password

Two kinds of seeded database exist.

**Yours (`build_db`).** The users of `USERS` (at least two), each with its login name and its password stored EXACTLY as
typed at login in the users table: the login must succeed for a row whose password column holds that plain text, and
the answers never carry it. `seed_rows()` is where the rows are written; they must satisfy the route check of section 10.
On SQLite `build_db` writes the schema by hand in plain SQL (the `DDL` string), identical to what the service itself
creates on an empty file (`python3 smoke.py OUT <x> schema` prints it), then the rows.

**The checking environment's own** (used when the service has a SQLite provider). It starts your
service on an empty SQLite file once, lets it create its schema, deletes every row the service wrote at start-up, then
inserts rows itself by plain SQL, without calling the service, and then logs in through your login route. The users it
writes are `admin`, `alice`, `bob` and `carol`; the login name is `<handle>@example.com` (for example
`alice@example.com`, so the login-name column must accept at least 40 characters), the password is `<handle>-pass-0031`
(for example `alice-pass-0031`), and the password column holds that text exactly as typed, as for yours. A second
database for a re-probe uses `-pass-0097`, other row counts and other integer keys: depend on no id. Every other column
gets a placeholder (text such as `Name 01`, integers, 0/1 for booleans, timestamps as text `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff`
in UTC, foreign keys pointing at rows it inserted), respecting NOT NULL and uniqueness. The users table has a text column
that holds the login name, named like the login body's username field or the first unique text column of the table.

## 9. Background services

When the spec names a background service, `SERVICES[name](db)` answers a `ServiceCmd(argv, env, cwd, stop_timeout)`:
how that service starts on the scenario's database (`db` is a SQLite path, or the clone's URL on MySQL). An `Await` step
of a scenario starts it on that scenario's database, polls the database about every 0.2 s until the step's `expect_db`
holds (within the step's seconds it passes, else a finding), and stops it (its process group: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL
after `stop_timeout`) whatever happened. The service runs with the caller's environment plus `ServiceCmd.env`; it gets
no `PORT`. It is a separate process: the skeleton starts the same built assembly with the argument `worker`; how your
program reacts to an argument is yours. The service's database access must commit each change (the checker reads the
database from outside). `smoke.py` starts every `SERVICES` entry on the seeded SQLite file for 2 seconds and fails if it
exits with an error.

## 10. The route check, and `truth.json`

For every route of `truth.json` the environment makes one call:

- every `{...}` segment of the route's `template` is replaced by `1`: path parameters are integer row ids;
- a `POST`, `PUT` or `PATCH` carries the JSON body `{}`;
- the caller is the first user of `USERS` whose role in `truth.json` `seed_users` matches the route's `auth` (`Member`
  or `Admin`); a `Public` route is called without credentials;
- order: all `GET`s, then the writes, then the `DELETE`s.

The status must be neither `404` nor `405`, which is what an unregistered route answers. A `404` that your own code
answers for a missing row is not told apart from it. So `build_db` must seed, for each table a path parameter names, a row
with id `1` that the calling user may reach (it belongs to that user, directly or through its parents), and the parent
rows it needs. The environment also calls each non-public route without credentials and expects `401` or `403` (a
warning, not a failure). If your brief fixes the rows of the seed, `build_db` writes exactly those and no more; a
path-parameter route then may answer `404` for the missing row, and `python3 smoke.py OUT <x> --warn-404` prints it as a
warning instead of a failure.

`smoke.py` reads only these keys of `truth.json` (its full schema is in your brief): `routes[{method, template, auth,
file, line}]`, `seed_users[{name, role}]` (one per login name of `USERS`, roles `Member` or `Admin`) and `login.path`
(a public `POST` route in `routes`).

## 11. `studio.toml`, and how the harness module is imported

```toml
[app]
app = "tests.spec.<x>_harness:make_app"
db = "tests.spec.<x>_harness:build_db"
runtime = "tests.spec.<x>_harness:RUNTIME"
```

Keys of the table `[app]` that Lattice reads: `app`, `db`, `runtime` (always), and `login`
(`"tests.spec.<x>_harness:LOGIN"`, when a function other than the runtime's is the login), `services`
(`"tests.spec.<x>_harness:SERVICES"`, when there are background services), `database` (`"mysql"` or `"sqlite"`; absent:
`sqlite`), `login_path`, `database_url`. Use only the keys your brief asks for.

The DOTTED module form `tests.spec.<x>_harness:<attribute>` is required. The bare form `<x>_harness:make_app` cannot be
imported by the environment (it answers `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '<x>_harness'`; checked). The dotted form
resolves because the environment runs from the repository root, which is on `sys.path`: `tests/` has NO `__init__.py`
(a namespace package) and `tests/spec/` has one (an empty file, already in the repository). So create neither.

The harness runs inside Lattice's Python process: `lattice` is importable there, and so are `httpx` and, for MySQL,
PyMySQL. Import only the standard library and those names; the harness prints nothing on import.

FAILS: list[str] = []
WARN_404 = "--warn-404" in sys.argv
if WARN_404:
    sys.argv.remove("--warn-404")


def ok(name: str, cond: bool, detail: str = "") -> bool:
    print(("PASS  " if cond else "FAIL  ") + name + (f"   -- {detail}" if detail and not cond else ""))
    if not cond:
        FAILS.append(name)
    return bool(cond)
